payload.authority: researcher decision under the preregistration's own amendment clause, taken before the calibration partition was read and before Stage 0 was run

calibration_preregistration.bounds.uniqu.after: resolve_numeric_bounds() is the single path. Native numeric bounds come from the lock; string bounds require a declared interpretation whose value must EXACTLY equal float(frozen literal). The resulting 20-dimension map is hashed as bounds_resolution_hash and frozen, so the bounds the optimizer uses are reconstructible from frozen artifacts alone.
calibration_preregistration.bounds.uniqu.before: (did not exist) The three string upper bounds frozen in the lock had declared numeric interpretations, but nothing guaranteed that the optimizer's bounds came from that declaration rather than from some second computation.

calibration_preregistration.data.first_a.after: Append-only ledger data/splits/calibration_access_ledger.json with an explicit definition of what counts as an access (reading recording VALUES counts; hashing the recording-id set does not), the point of first access (stage 1 start), and an ordering rule: a count > 0 with no frozen stage 0 artifact means the preregistered order was violated and the run must stop. CP-16 checks the count is 0 at freeze time.
calibration_preregistration.data.first_a.before: (did not exist) held-out had an auditable access_count; the calibration partition had only the sentence "not read yet".

calibration_preregistration.dimension_ex.after: Explicit expansion map. _ALBEDO_BY_PRESET expands to {.water, .bubbly, .misty} with shared_bounds: true. Any fitted parameter whose initial value is a dict or list and has no declared expansion is REFUSED, so this class of ambiguity cannot recur silently. PARTICIPATING_MEDIA is therefore 6 dimensions, not 4.
calibration_preregistration.dimension_ex.before: (did not exist) Stages listed registry parameter names only, so _ALBEDO_BY_PRESET -- three independent class-specific scalars -- was ambiguous between 1 and 3 search dimensions, which directly changes the population size and therefore the budget.

calibration_preregistration.optimizer.ev.after: maxiter: 100 and the budget is DERIVED, not estimated: P(N) = 2**ceil(log2(popsize * N)); budget_per_restart(N) = P(N) * (maxiter + 1); budget_per_stage(N) = restarts * budget_per_restart(N). Resolved: AMBIENT 2d/P32/9696, SIGNAL_SCALE 2d/P32/9696, GEOMETRY_SURFACE_FOIL 7d/P128/38784, PARTICIPATING_MEDIA 6d/P128/38784, SENSOR_SURROGATE 3d/P64/19392; total 116352 evaluations. The runner counts evaluations itself and aborts the stage with NOT_CONVERGED on the (budget+1)-th call.
calibration_preregistration.optimizer.ev.before: max_evaluations_per_stage: 3000 together with maxiter: 200 and restarts: 3 -- mutually unsatisfiable for every stage. Measured on scipy 1.15.3: N=2 -> 4192, N=3 -> 11584, N=4 -> 12864, N=7 -> 25728 function evaluations, i.e. up to 8.6x the stated per-stage budget for a single restart and 25.7x across three. Root cause: popsize was treated as the population size, but it is a MULTIPLIER, and init='sobol' additionally rounds the population up to a power of two.

calibration_preregistration.optimizer.me.after: Exactly one solver path: every stage is solved by differential_evolution over all of that stage's expanded dimensions. The scalar path is removed entirely; CP-07 fails if scalar_stages reappears.
calibration_preregistration.optimizer.me.before: scalar_stages.applies_to listed three PARAMETERS (ambient_energy_to_mcps, signal_energy_to_mcps, sigma_width_to_mm) while multivariate_stages applied to STAGES, leaving no answer to "is stage 1, which has two parameters, solved scalar-wise or jointly?"

calibration_preregistration.s_f_relative.after: Retained as a NON-GATING diagnostic computed at stage 1 start, after s_f has been legitimately produced by calibration first access. It is recorded in artifacts and may never change any stage's parameter set.
calibration_preregistration.s_f_relative.before: (did not exist; the s_f question was the admission gate)

calibration_preregistration.stage_0.admi.after: leverage_sim(p, o) = |o(p=hi) - o(p=lo)| / sigma_MC(o), admit if >= 10, where sigma_MC is the seed-to-seed standard deviation of the observable over R=8 independent simulation seeds at the frozen initial parameter values. Values in [5, 20] are BORDERLINE and halt with STAGE0_ADJUDICATION_REQUIRED rather than being auto-classified. Stage 0 is now simulation-only in fact, not only in its declaration.
calibration_preregistration.stage_0.admi.before: leverage(p, o) = |delta o| / s_f(o), admit if >= 0.5, where s_f is the pooled IQR of the CALIBRATION SPLIT's real values -- while the same stage declared reads_calibration_partition: false

calibration_preregistration.stage_0.coll.after: response vectors normalised component-wise by sigma_MC before the cosine, making the number unit-free. An unnormalised cosine over components with different physical units changes value when the units change, so the 0.98 threshold was not well defined.
calibration_preregistration.stage_0.coll.before: cosine similarity of raw observable response vectors (unit-dependent)

calibration_preregistration.stagewise.GE.after: Corrected wording plus a line-by-line code citation. The audit finding is that the CODE IS CORRECT: scene["bottle_interior"] is built UNCONDITIONALLY for all four classes; only interior["interior"] = medium is conditional, via _medium_dict(), and _DENSITY_KEY_BY_PRESET has no "empty" key. _INTERIOR_BASE_IOR["empty"] = "air". Measured construction: all four classes carry bottle_interior with r_in = 26.5 mm, r_out = 28.5 mm (wall 2.0 mm); Empty has int_ior=air, ext_ior=bk7 and no participating medium. Empty is glass shell + air + glass shell. This was a PREREGISTRATION WORDING DEFECT, not a code regression, so the frozen initial_simulation.lock is unaffected.
calibration_preregistration.stagewise.GE.before: "build_scene_dict() only builds the interior medium when medium_preset != 'empty'" -- wording nearly identical to the sentence NOTE-029 used to describe the SOLID-GLASS-CYLINDER DEFECT, and therefore readable as "Empty has no interior cylinder".

invariants_preserved.bounds_unchanged: every fitted parameter's [lo, hi] is still exactly the frozen initial_simulation.lock range; this amendment resolves how the three string bounds are read, it does not widen or narrow any bound
invariants_preserved.fitted_parameter_set_unchanged: 18 registry parameters (now stated as 20 optimizer dimensions)
invariants_preserved.s_f_definition_unchanged: calibration-only pooled IQR, computed once and frozen
invariants_preserved.stagewise_structure_unchanged: 5 stages in the same order with the same identifiability arguments
invariants_preserved.weights_unchanged: UNIFORM 1.0 over 16 class x feature terms

precondition_evidence.disclosure_no_results_exist: No calibration objective value has ever been computed, for any parameter setting, so there is no result this amendment could have been shaped to favour. The three defects were found by auditing the frozen protocol against the code and against scipy's measured behaviour.

payload.rationale:
## P0-1: why option A (make stage 0 genuinely simulation-only), not option B (redefine stage 0 as calibration-data-consuming).
The defect is real and structural: v0.1.0 declared stage_0.reads_calibration_partition = false while its only admission rule divided by s_f, which is defined in the same document as the pooled IQR of the calibration split's REAL values. The stage could not have been executed as written without first reading the partition.
Option B was rejected on two independent grounds.
(1) LEAKAGE. Under B, the SET OF PARAMETERS THAT GET FITTED would be chosen using real calibration data. That is a data-dependent model-selection step sitting upstream of every subsequent stage, and its effect is not captured by any of the existing guards -- the verification-seed check tests seed overfitting, not selection bias. It would also move calibration first access earlier for no scientific gain, since nothing in stage 0's actual question requires real data.
(2) IDENTIFIABILITY. The question stage 0 must answer is "can the optimizer distinguish this parameter's effect from noise?". For a Monte-Carlo simulator the relevant noise floor is its own seed-to-seed dispersion, not the real data's IQR. Under CRN the within-stage objective is deterministic, so a parameter whose full-range effect is below sigma_MC produces a fitted value that is an artefact of the chosen seeds -- exactly the failure that verification seeds would flag as SEED_OVERFIT only AFTER an entire stage's budget had been spent. sigma_MC pre-empts it. Using s_f would instead have answered "does this parameter matter to J", which is a legitimate but DIFFERENT question, and one that belongs in a diagnostic rather than a gate.
The s_f question is therefore not discarded: it survives as s_f_relative_leverage_diagnostic, computed at stage 1 start and explicitly forbidden from changing any parameter set.
Threshold choice: K = 10 with R = 8 replicates means a full-range sweep must move an observable by ten seed-to-seed standard deviations, i.e. about 10*sqrt(8) ~= 28 standard errors of the mean. K was fixed before any measurement. The [5, 20] borderline band halts rather than rounding, on the same principle as the estimator round's TIE_BREAK_REQUIRED: if the probe cannot separate, the honest output is that it cannot separate.
## P0-2: why the budget is derived rather than stated.
v0.1.0's three budget numbers could not all be true at once, and the error was not small -- it was a factor of 8.6 to 25.7. A stated budget that the optimizer silently blows through is worse than no budget, because "evaluations used" then carries no information. The remedy is to derive the budget from scipy's actual population rule, publish the resolved table in the protocol, have CP-13 compare the table against the formula item by item, and have the runner enforce it with a guard that aborts on the (budget+1)-th call rather than reporting the overrun afterwards. The honest consequence -- roughly 65 single-threaded hours at ~2 s per evaluation -- is disclosed in the protocol so that "the budget is not affordable" is discovered before the run, not during it.
## P1-3: the code was audited, not assumed.
The wording defect was found by reading build_scene_dict() line by line and then constructing all four scenes and inspecting the resulting dictionaries. Empty is a glass shell with an air interior. No STOP condition applies, no calibration is blocked, and the frozen initial_simulation.lock is unaffected.

payload.title: Fix three pre-execution defects in the calibration preregistration: a stage-0 criterion that secretly required calibration data, an optimizer budget that understated the real cost by 8.6-25.7x, and wording that echoed the already-fixed Empty solid-glass topology bug
